🗣️ 'We were able to bounce back, but we need to look at the things we have not done so well'Nuno Espirito Santo reflects on West Ham's performance after the Hammers fought back from 2-0 down to draw with Millwall. pic.twitter.com/NM1wQVcN0o

Asked by Sky Sports for his view on the “spitting” incident, Alex Neil said: “Fil [Marschall] was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened at that point... Obviously I’m so far away it’s hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn’t presume that Fil would say that without cause.

“I’m sure the referee and authorities who need to deal with it will look at it and, if it warrants it, it needs dealt with and then I’m sure they will.”

"It's one of the best atmospheres I've ever played in..I got shivers walking out"Millwall's Caleb Taylor speaks to Aaron Paul following today's 2-2 draw with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/yFoRuxooe6

Will there be one final chance? Sturge earns a throw-in on the far side and Dykes limbers up... But West Ham clear their lines and that is that. It ends two goals apiece.

Lisbie has looked dangerous down that left side and he just runs out of room under pressure from Mavropanos. The pair square up, with Lisbie sticking his finger into the Greek’s cheek.

Lisbie darts to the by-line but his cutback does not make it through the thicket of limbs and West Ham clear their lines.

Millwall earn a free-kick to the left of the box as Mavropanos climbs all over Dykes. Servais picks out Baggott at the far post and his knock-down lands to Dykes who, will spinning, strikes the ball over the bar.

DYKES! 😱So close to a late winner for Millwall, but his shot flies over the bar. pic.twitter.com/fQFpQBdS7j

Neghli steps up to take it but it strikes the wall.

There will be five minutes of time added on...

Woah.. Kante gets his pocket picked by Lisbie on the half-way line and the West Ham goalscorer has no choice but to foul him as the last man. West Ham have a free-kick just outside the box.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs

Millwall have put so much into this and it’s starting to tell. Their players look leggy and aren’t able to track Kante’s run into the channel though Cooper is just about able to clear his lines. Bowen’s corner comes to nothing.

Millwall 2 West Ham 1 (Kante) The substitute strokes a right-footed effort into the bottom corner from outside the box. A great finish.

Chance! Bowen stands up a delightful cross and Pablo forces Marschall into a fine stop. Corner awarded.

Some confusion here as Marschall appears to have taken too long over a goal-kick, and while most believe that a West Ham corner had been awarded, it ends up being a goal-kick.

The ITV commentators say that West Ham are alleging that Marschall spat in Pablo’s direction.

Arconte chases down a lost cause and telescopes a leg through Taylor to earn a corner. He spins around to the home supporters and windmills his arms in their direction as the volume increases. Metcalfe’s cross is well overhit, though, and sails out for a goal-kick.

Kante’s runs in behind are threatening to disrupt Millwall’s backline shape, but Neil’s midfield sentries Mazou-Sacko and Metcalfe are doing such a great job to cover the gaps that the hosts still look like they have things under control.

Oof. Metcalfe leaves a foot in on Morato, his studs going into the defender’s Achilles. He should perhaps consider himself lucky to avoid punishment there. One that VAR may have intervened on in the Premier League.

Penalty shout! Metcalfe drives forward into the right of the box and Kante, who is hot pursuit, pushes the midfielder to the ground. Tierney immediately waves away the appeals and replays concur that the contact is probably not strong enough to warrant a penalty.

Bowen is presented with some grass to run into but his cross is well cleared. He gets another bite at the cherry, trying his luck from the edge of the box and Marschall just about gets to the rebound ahead of an onrushing Kante. A corner is awarded which the Millwall stopper flaps at but his team-mates are able to avert the danger.

West Ham earn a chance to deliver a corner from the near side but Engel’s inswinger finds Marschall’s gloves. Really poor.

Millwall continue leveraging Cooper and Taylor’s height in the box off set-pieces. Here, Metcalfe’s free-kick skims off the top of Cooper’s head but just misses the mark.

It looks like West Ham have gone to three at the back as Kante joins Mukasa and Engels in midfield. He’ll look to make late runs in behind.

Two changes from Nuno, who takes off Piroe and Walker-Peters for Pablo and Kante.

Millwall have been good value for their lead, taking 16 shots and creating three big chances. West Ham, conversely have managed just one shot, off-target, despite controlling two-thirds of possession.

Arne Engel’s heatmap suggests he’s spent most of the match inside or just in advance of West Ham’s defensive third, which is not where Nuno will want either him or Divine Mukasa. The West Ham head coach could be tempted into changes at the break.

This is no more than Millwall – and West Ham – deserve. Sykes’s outrageous 35-yard strike deserved a goal and Neghli makes sure justice is served on the stroke of half-time. The roar that greets the players leaving the field is deafening.

The Den is in dreamland. Millwall take a two-goal advantage into the break and Neil celebrates with unbridled delight on the touchline. A caveat, though... Millwall did spurn a 2-0 lead in their most recent match away at Middlesbrough.

Millwall 2 West Ham 0 (Neghli) It’s come from yet another Dykes long throw, which West Ham have failed to clear. The ball falls to the feet of Neghli in the six-yard box and he spears the ball beyond Hermansen and Bowen on the line. And that’s the half.

Another foul... Osei-Tutu jumps into Morato but West Ham give the free-kick straight back to their opponents.

It’s seven-seven in the fouls contest for those wondering, the latest being a mistimed challenge on Sykes by Castellanos near the right touchline. Millwall pump another ball into the box which is not up to much.

In an attempt to get his foot on the ball, Engels has often peeled out to the right-back position, but a wild, desperate cross-field ball that goes straight to Osei-Tutu sums up West Ham’s half aptly.

A wild challenge from Metcalfe on Cooper earns West Ham a free-kick and its then Sykes’ turn to land a late tackle, this time in the right channel. The subsequent delivery finds Castellanos but he cannot direct the ball goalwards.

West Ham’s strength comes from the fluidity of their front four, but Nuno’s creators have not been able to access them. So effective has Millwall’s back-line coverage been that West Ham have only managed low-quality final-third entries.

For the first time this half, Millwall begin to retreat deep into their own half, their lines of defence merging. And while West Ham tot up a fair number of passes on the edge of the box, they ultimately cede possession and Millwall spring a counter. Arconte appears to be through but Kilman does well to recover and Dykes’ subsequent shot is charged down.

Millwall are going man-to-man as West Ham try to build and the visitors are struggling to get out. Sturge works infield from his starting perch on the left and almost threads a through-ball in behind for Arconte to gallop on to but Kilman does well to stick in a boot.

West Ham are desperately trying to calm this game down, but the Millwall fans are making that quite the challenge. The visitors string a series of passes together before Bowen strays offside.

Millwall then burst forward, Arconte this time popping up in a dangerous position on the right but Metcalfe fires over having picked off a loose Hammers pass out from the back.

Another Dykes throw-in sparks panic in West Ham’s box. Osei-Tutu’s back-post header appears to take a deflection off Walker-Peters, but the referee awards a goal-kick.

Millwall 1 West Ham 0 (Taylor) If at first you don’t succeed, try and try again... Dykes’ long throw from the right prompts chaos on the West Ham box and although Hermansen is able to keep out efforts from Sykes and Arconte, he can’t deny Taylor from close range. Cue bedlam in the stands. A massive, massive goal.

Or not… The Den erupts! That was appalling defending from a long throw and West Ham got exactly what they deserved, with Mads Hemansen’s brilliant save failing to spare them.

MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D

It is all Millwall so far. They have been first to pretty much every ball and are giving West Ham no time on it at all. Konstantinos Mavropanos has just bought the visitors a breather after going down injured.

Hermansen gets caught in no-man’s land as Millwall spin in another ball from deep. It falls to the feet of Dykes but his effort does not have the requisite power to beat Kilman on the line.

Mavropanos appears to have been taken out by his own goalkeeper in the commotion and receives some on-field medical treatment.

Neil will be happy with how his side have started this match. Their intensity off the ball has forced West Ham into errors and here Sturge picks Bowen’s pocket on the halfway line before picking out Arconte in the box. He tries to squeeze a shot through Mukasa but the young midfielder does well to clear his lines.

The resulting corner comes out to Mazou-Sacko on the edge of the box but his effort sails over the bar.

Dykes and Arconte are Millwall’s attacking threats and the former wins a free-kick in the left channel. The hosts load the box with their biggest aerial threats but Metcalfe’s teasing inswinger just evades everyone. Tierney blows up for a foul anyhow...

There’s a minor clash off the ball as Morato and Cooper exchange words. Paul Tierney speaks with both players before Dykes launches a long throw into the box which is cleared and Hermansen is wise to the subsequent cross off the second phase.

Arconte tiptoes into the West Ham box and picks out Sturge whose miscued shot finds Metcalfe on the edge of the box. His effort is straight at Hermansen who collects the ball calmly.

That Jenson Metcalfe tackle on West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen came after just 15 seconds. What Vinny Jones might call “a reducer”.

"That's the expectation, I would imagine" 😅The first free-kick is awarded just 12 seconds into Millwall's derby against West Ham.Watch it LIVE on ITV1 🎥 pic.twitter.com/qpxjQEKN6x

Millwall launch a free-kick from deep into the box after Castellanos gives away a needless foul and after some pinball Hermansen gathers.

It took just 13 seconds for us to get our first foul. Kudos to anyone who had that in their Dockers Derby sweepstake... A late lunge from Metcalfe on Bowen.

And the players emerge, Hey Jude now being played... Millwall are in their customary navy-blue home strip and white shorts. West Ham are giving their new white away kit a first outing.

There’s just about enough time for the two sides to meet for quick summits before Millwall get us under way!

The atmosphere is building nicely in the ground and the players are now lined up in the tunnel, Cooper and Bowen standing shoulder to shoulder.

Seats are filling up rapidly with barely 10 minutes before kick-off, with the away end a notable exception. The home fans are making their own presence felt as The Jam’s A Town Called Malice and The Clash’s London Calling blare out over the public-address system.

"The fans are up for it, the players are up for it" 💪🏼Lyndon Dykes looks ahead to today's match, and reflects on his strong start to life as a Millwall player.Watch it LIVE on ITV1 🎥 pic.twitter.com/V9nPzbh3Ob

Kevin Nolan, West Ham’s captain, was sent off early but his team-mates defied the odds to win 2-1 thanks to goals from Carlton Cole and Winston Reid either side of a stunning Liam Trotter strike.

In Millwall’s match-day squad that day were… Harry Kane and Ryan Mason.

The last time West Ham and Millwall met, Harry Kane was a Millwall player 😅This is how that game in 2012 played out 👇 pic.twitter.com/OhtVx3caCP

This rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

“There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” says Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”

Though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

“It really is about the hooligan era,” says a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”

Jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd

There have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

At the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at New Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

The hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police said that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means…

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

When asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno said: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [important], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

On potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”

The gaffer on tomorrow's fixture ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/6NG6t4t4Fn

#westham on the way to #millwall via #london bridge #whufc #coyi pic.twitter.com/HrWgJ6UtJY

Riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

The game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

The Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

Alex Neil switches out goalkeeper Max Crocombe for Filip Marschall and names the returning Mathis Servais, Kyrell Lisbie and Alfie Doughty on the bench.

Alex Neil names his Lions XI 👊 pic.twitter.com/MP0N9wMatG

Just the one change from the league leaders’ last league match as Kyle Walker-Peters comes in for the injured Joel Veltman.

Today's teamsheet 📋 pic.twitter.com/EmrxYRhsPd

"We have to quiet them down" 🤫West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen is expecting a hostile atmosphere at The Den today 🗣️Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/9tp2225Rq8

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

Acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

Much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

#1471. Time to take Portugal seriously again? Stats since 2022 show why Cristiano Ronaldo retirement could be a blessing

Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football after 23 years with Portugal. But is the national side actually stronger without him? We’ve crunched the numbers.

Ronaldo bowed out as his country’s record goalscorer, having scored 146 goals in 234 appearances. In his retirement announcement, he spoke of “handing back the number seven shirt” after more than two decades representing his country. Portugal fans can bet on soccer at Bovada.

In 234 international appearances, he scored 146 goals and provided 45 assists, averaging a goal contribution every 97.4 minutes.

With those sorts of numbers, it begs the question of why people would think that Ronaldo is now a hindrance to his country, rather than one of their biggest assets.

This narrative started to gain prominence around the 2022 World Cup, when CR7 found himself in a rut for both club and country.

He only scored one goal during that tournament and his understudy, Goncalo Ramos, was looking sharper at the time.

This led to Ronaldo being benched for Portugal’s quarter-final clash against Morocco, which they ultimately lost 1-0.

Many predicted that was the end for Ronaldo on the international stage, but that couldn’t have been further from the truth.

Roberto Martinez put Ronaldo front and centre, leading to two underwhelming tournament performances and early exits.

Ronaldo has now finally called time on his international career, with his announcement following a turbulent period involving new manager Jorge Jesus.

With a lot of discourse currently around Ronaldo and Portugal, we’ve compared the national team results with and without him since the 2022 World Cup.

Since then, Portugal have played a total of 49 matches. Of those, CR7 has featured in 37 and has missed 12.

In the games Ronaldo has played, Portugal have boasted a win percentage of 70.2% and have scored an average of 2.05 goals per game.

Without Ronaldo, Portugal’s win percentage is higher at 75% and their goal-per-game ratio jumps to 3.41.

Of course, the sample size of games without Ronaldo is small, meaning that the odd freak result will have a larger impact on the numbers.

For example, Ronaldo didn’t feature in Portugal’s 9-0 hammering of Luxembourg back in 2023, which boosts the numbers quite a bit in this regard.

But the direction of travel in late 2026 is clear. Here’s the full breakdown of what the stats say:

Win percentage: 70.2% Loss percentage: 13.5%

Goals per game: 2.05 (78) Goals against per game: 0.63 (24) ⭐

Win percentage: 75%⭐ Loss percentage: 8.3%⭐

#1465. Cristiano Ronaldo’s 143 international goals: Could any of these five players surpass him?

Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his international retirement and set a very high bar for the top goalscorer of all time.

After 234 caps, Ronaldo confirmed that he was retiring from the Portuguese national team and does so having scored 146 goals for the team in a 23-year stint.

That tally puts him top of the all-time scorers for their national team with the also-retired Lionel Messi next best with 20 fewer goals.

Ali Daei of Iran makes up the top three but are there any players who could beat Ronaldo’s record?

The current highest-ranked active player is Lukaku who has scored 94 goals for Belgium.

His age, however, makes it very difficult for him to reach Ronaldo’s tally. Lukaku is 33 now and scores at a rate of 0.7 per match, that means he needs another 76 matches to score 147 goals.

He plays between 5-10 international games per year and so would need to play for another seven years or so which would take him to the age Ronaldo is now.

It’s not impossible but is unlikely you would figure.

If you’re looking for a 33-year-old who could break the record then ignore Lukaku and instead focus on Kane.

The reason why Kane is a more tempting bet is he is in ridiculous goal scoring form, the kind of form that wins you the Ballon d’Or.

Kane’s got 91 in 125 England games, meaning he’s at 0.73 per match, his numbers though have really ramped up in the last five seasons.

He got 16 in 2021, including four in the delayed Euro 2020, and 13 in 2026 with more games yet to come.

If he continues at the rate of his career so far, he would need 77 more matches but he has a one-in-one record for 2026. Continue at that pace and he would reach the tally a lot quicker.

If you were a betting man, you would probably put your money on Mbappe to be the one to reach it.

He’s got a lot of good things going for him. First of all, he’s the main goalscoring output for a nation that regularly reaches major tournament finals. Secondly, he’s incredibly good in those tournaments and has won the Golden Boot in the last two World Cups. Thirdly, he’s only 27.

Mbappe’s goal-scoring rate overall is a little lower than Kane or Lukaku’s but he is making up for any lost time. The Real Madrid forward has got 12 in 13 2026 games. In 2022 and 2023, he broke double digits and since moving centrally, he has only scored more for his club side.

Mbappe has got 67 goals from his 107 games, putting him 78 behind Ronaldo but you would fancy him to get close at the least by the time his career is over.

READ: Will Cristiano Ronaldo get a Portugal farewell match? What we know after retirement announcement

Haaland’s goalscoring ratio makes him a strong contender.

The Norwegian machine has a better-than-a-goal-a-game ratio for his country and, while meaning no disrespect to Norway, he is doing it in not one of the elite nations.

Haaland has got 65 in 59 including five in seven at the most recent World Cup and has age on his side as well with him being 26.

Where Haaland may fall down is that he does not play for one of the top nations and so reaching tournaments and then going deep in them is not a given.

The 2026 World Cup was the first time Norway have appeared in it in 28 years and while you would say they are one of the 48 best teams in the world right now, that could fluctuate more than other nations like France, Germany and Spain.

He’s got a long way to go, but he certainly has the time to get there.

Yamal has 11 goals for Spain so far, putting him a whopping 135 goals behind Ronaldo but Yamal is only 19, meaning he has another 22 years in the game if he were to play to the age of Ronaldo.

Although one of the most impressive attributes about both Ronaldo and Messi is their longevity. Yamal would not be the first young superstar to be off the top perch by the time he was 30.

One other negative for Yamal is he is not an out-and-out goalscorer in the same way Ronaldo in particular was. Yamal got just one goal and four assists in Euro 2024 while he failed to really shine in the 2026 World Cup despite Spain winning it.

If he begins to score more goals, especially for the national team, and if he stays healthy, he could do it but those are two big ifs.

#1463. The top goalscorers for club & country in 2026 so far: Kane, Yamal, Mbappe, Raphinha…

Big names from Real Madrid, Barcelona, Arsenal and Bayern Munich feature alongside some surprise names in the most prolific goalscorers of the calendar year so far.

Some big names are surprisingly absent from the most prolific goalscorers of 2026 to date.

Drawn from Europe’s five major leagues, here are the top 10 goalscorers in 2026 across club and international competitions.

Schick has had reason to celebrate in 2026. Earlier this year, he reached the milestone of 100 goals for Bayer Leverkusen.

He’s been on fire this season, with 11 goals from 13 games for the German side.

There won’t be any more international goals from Schick, though. He retired from Czech Republic duty after the World Cup.

The jury is still out on Gyokeres, who remains a perplexing forward.

This calendar year has seen him look borderline anonymous and increasingly sidelined at Arsenal.

And yet Gyokeres also fired Sweden to the World Cup with a hat-trick against Ukraine and a late winner against Poland. He’s basically the Ikea Gerd Muller at this point.

Dembele has scored 20 goals in 36 PSG appearances this year, including several crucial strikes in Europe – none bigger than the equalising spot kick he coolly dispatched against Arsenal in the Champions League final.

His goal in France’s World Cup win over Iraq was, incredibly, his first in major tournament football. That was swiftly followed up with a rapid hat-trick against Norway, before another in the quarter-final against Morocco.

He is largely taking it easy right now, once again frequently rested during PSG’s domestic campaign. But he popped up with a goal against Manchester City.

What a year it’s been for Malen. Started it as a benchwarmer at Aston Villa. Set to finish it as one of Europe’s most lethal strikers at Roma.

Malen made an immediate impact after his January move to the Italian capital and his scoring rate has barely slowed down since.

For some reason, his form hasn’t quite translated into international football; he hasn’t scored for the Netherlands at all this year.

But high-flying Roma are laughing. Malen almost won the Serie A golden boot last season despite arriving midway through and he’s a leading contender for the gong this season.

A fairly recent entrant into the top 10 after heading into the international break on the back of a hat trick against Union Berlin.

Olise was the Bundesliga’s best assister last season but has been more than capable of finding the net himself a fair few times too.

He didn’t score any goals at the World Cup but netted the winner in Zinedine Zidane’s second game in charge of France. The best Fantasy Footballer around right now.

Yamal has long been talked up as a Ballon d’Or contender, and slowly but surely he’s getting the numbers to back it up.

The teenager’s goalscoring output has grown season on season, and 2025-26 was no exception. February’s hat-trick against Villarreal was evidence of a player about to go truly stratospheric.

Unfortunately, the final furlong of the campaign was hit by a hamstring injury, or else we suspect he’d be a few places higher up in this list.

He needed just 10 minutes in his first World Cup start to find the back of the net, although that would be his only goal in Spain’s triumph out in North America.

Now he’s looking fit and hungry – at least based on the evidence of his exceptional form of late.

The Brazilian has an exceptional tally of 33 goals for Barcelona so far this calendar year (plus one for Brazil), which is especially impressive when you consider he’s missed quite a lot of action due to injury.

He averages a goal every 49 minutes for Barca this season – to put that in context, Kylian Mbappe averages a goal every 84 minutes for Real Madrid.

Raphinha has scored in all but three of the Barca games he’s played in in 2026-27, scoring hat tricks in two, and currently leads the Europe-wide goalscoring charts with 15 in the league.

The top three are the last three winners of the European Golden Shoe. This list has taken a while to take shape, but the frontrunners are the usual suspects.

Haaland’s four goals against Iraq and Senegal in the group stages finally saw him climb up into the top 10, from which he was surprisingly absent in the latter half of the 2025-26 club season, before he added to his World Cup tally against the Ivory Coast. Then there were two goals against Brazil.

He finally drew a blank as Norway exited the World Cup at the hands of England at the quarter-final stage. He earned a well-deserved rest before spearheading Man City’s new era under Enzo Maresca.

Same as it ever was with nine goals in nine Premier League appearances for City this season, plus braces against Porto and PSG and another Champions League goal against his favourite opponents, RB Leipzig.

Like his rival Haaland, it somehow took Mbappe until mid-June to enter the top 10.

Mbappe kicked off the year in superb style, scoring in six successive starts for Real Madrid (nine goals in total) before dipping considerably with just one goal in his next seven appearances.

By the nature of his 10 goals at the World Cup, we don’t expect to see the Real Madrid superstar dropping back out. His Champions League record is pretty sensational.

Arguably the finest player in world football right now. How often have you been able to say that about an Englishman?

The only player in Europe’s five major leagues to average a better-than-goal-a-game output so far this calendar year, the England captain has 41 goals in 40 appearances for Bayern Munich in all competitions in 2026 – including home and away against Real Madrid and PSG.

He capped off his superb season with a hat-trick in the DFB Pokal final. Two goals against Croatia showed Kane carried his form into the World Cup, where he eventually scored six times.

Unbelievably, the Norway game was Kane’s first knockout appearance for club and country in 2025-26 in which he didn’t score. Which, of course, he followed with a blank against Argentina.

Surprisingly enough, Kane failed to add to his tally by drawing a blank in his first three Bayern appearances of the 2026-27 campaign.

But it’s back to normal service with his Bayern tally standing at 10 goals in 14 games. The Czechs and Croatia have been on the receiving end in the Nations League too.

Still some way to go before catching Lionel Messi’s calendar year record, mind.

#1461. Nicky Butt doubles down on Michael Carrick's 'management's not for me' claim - as he pinpoints moment under-fire Man United boss made comment

Published: 07:20 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 07:21 EDT, 3 November 2026

Former Manchester United star Nicky Butt has doubled down on his bizarre claim that Michael Carrick told him 'management's not for me' before he took the job at Old Trafford.

Carrick, 45, returned to the club where he earned legendary status as a player in January in the aftermath of Ruben Amorim's sacking.

Despite a strong end to last season when he guided United to third place, Carrick is under huge pressure this time around after picking up just seven points from nine matches.

Speaking last month, Butt revealed that Carrick had told him he would only return to management for the United job after his sacking by Middlesbrough in June 2025, a claim the current Red Devils boss subsequently laughed off.

Yet, Butt, appearing on Football Uncensored with Piers Morgan, has reaffirmed his stance and pinpointed the exact moment when Carrick told him he didn't want to get back in the dugout.

'I believe I said that but I’ll clarify what I meant,' Butt said. 'And I’m not ducking it, I’m really not, I’ll explain. I was playing in a padel tournament with Michael, he’s my doubles partner, and I was talking about football and Middlesbrough.

Former Manchester United star Nicky Butt has doubled down on his bizarre claim that Michael Carrick told him 'management's not for me' before he took the job at Old Trafford

Speaking on Football Uncensored, Butt revealed the exact moment that Carrick made the claim

'I had a beer after it, and I was like "so what’s your plans mate? What do you think you’re going to do when you get back into management?"

'He said "no, it’s all over the show, it’s hard work – however, if the big one came up, obviously I would take it".'

Butt continued: 'And the big one did come up, and he took it, and that wasn’t a case of me saying Michael didn’t want the Man United job, it was a case of he didn’t want a job.

'He didn’t want to go driving up and down the M6 all day when he’s got kids at home for no reward.

'But if the big one comes, which I assume was Man United, then he’d take it. That’s the facts of the conversation that I had with him.'

When pressed on Butt's comments ahead of United's draw with Leeds last month, Carrick had said: 'I definitely wouldn't be here if that was the case, would I? At this stage, it's the best job and the best role I could possibly have.

'I feel a real privilege of being in this position and a real responsibility, but equally a drive of wanting to make a difference and having success here.

'I'm loving it. I love the situation when actually you get some sort of struggle and you've got to find a way out of it. I actually enjoy that because that's part of what drives you to have success.

'If you're not ready for that and you can't do anything that's difficult, then you're never going to be great. So we've got to work our way through it, and I'm enjoying it as we go.'

Butt claimed Carrick said he'd only return to management for 'the big job' at Man United

Butt's original claim had come on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast when he said: 'I was with Michael before he got the Man United job and spoke to him about management.

'He went "no it's not for me, it's too much, my head's all over the show, I'd only do it for the big job. The big job is Man United".

'So because that club's gone to him he's naturally going to go and do it. I think when he's gone through that door, put aside last year because like Scholesy said that's totally different to this year, I think he's realised he's gone into a club that's different to the club that he knew and was at.

'But these lads won't turn down Man United. Ole Gunnar (Solskjaer) wouldn't turn it down.

'Roy Keane might never turn that down. When that club comes calling and you've been at that football club, you don't turn it down.'

United and Carrick face a crunch week, with home games against Roma and Aston Villa coming ahead of next week's international break.

#1458. De Roon: “I never had any doubts about joining Roma.”

Marten De Roon gave an interview to Idealista.it in which he discussed his arrival in Rome.

“When the coach called me, I already knew it would be a difficult move, partly because of the history of Roma and Atalanta, partly because of my history with Roma on social media; but at a certain point we had made up our minds, I had no doubts. The pitch speaks for itself. I had no doubts; I wanted to prove on the pitch my desire to be here. Gasperini is also demonstrating this; facts count, there’s time.”

The Dutch midfielder explained how he experiences football: “In two different ways. On the pitch, I want to win at all costs. My main quality, what I like to do, is to see the game. I’m tactically prepared, it’s my strength: I see where we can attack well, where we can defend better. From midfield, I like to manage the team, call the markers. Off the pitch, I like to joke, talk, and, above all, observe. I like trying to help my teammates; I’m a professional, and even off the pitch, I try to be helpful, given my age and experience.”

The former Atalanta player spoke about the Giallorossi dressing room: “There are a lot of nice people. I’m still finding my role, so I don’t joke around too much, but the atmosphere is healthy; it seems like an ‘easy’ dressing room. Years ago, I thought it was a very difficult dressing room, even playing against them; now I’ve come in and I’ve seen that it’s healthy, warm, and welcoming. I already knew some of them, obviously Malen, Rensch, Mancini, Gollini, and Cristante. This obviously helps; it’s made things easier.”

De Roon gave a behind-the-scenes look at how he looked for a place to live in the capital: “I spoke to the guys here in the locker room, Pellegrini helped me get to know the city, he gave me a hand with so many things, together with the club.”

Marten De Roon spoke about his relationship with Gasperini: “We spent eight years together, we had the best time with Atalanta, we fought so many battles together, and I’ve always thanked him. Our relationship is above all professional; if he’s your coach, you don’t see him off the pitch during the week. Last year, he called me every now and then, asking about Malen, but more than anything he wanted confirmation; he was already convinced. I had no doubts. He’s doing pretty well, right?”

#1456. The 3 players in Europe who will earn more than Harry Kane after his new Bayern Munich deal

Harry Kane has signed a lucrative new contract with Bayern Munich on the back of his Ballon d’Or success and it’s said to be the biggest deal in the club’s history.

Kane was already among Europe’s highest earners and being recognised as the best player in the world last season will have helped him stay in that bracket.

There have even been some shouts that Kane is now Europe’s highest earner by base salary, but figures from Capology suggest otherwise.

And when bonuses are factored in, there are still some players potentially taking home more than the England captain.

Here are the players in Europe’s top five leagues with salaries worth more than Kane’s, which is estimated to be above £400,000 per week.

The runner-up to Kane in the 2026 Ballon d’Or stakes, Mbappe earns big bucks at Real Madrid.

It helped that they signed him on a free transfer from PSG, allowing them to pump more money towards his personal terms.

The word on the street is that Mbappe earns the equivalent of £508,399 per week as a base salary, but up to £1,165,983 with bonuses.

That’s a lot for someone who doesn’t win the Champions League. But he is pretty good, to be fair.

With Kane committing to Bayern until he’ll be nearing 36, the chances of him returning to the Premier League to become its all-time record scorer have just got a whole lot slimmer.

Over to you it is then, Mr Haaland, if anyone’s going to stand a chance of catching Alan Shearer’s record of 260.

He’s on 121 Premier League goals so far from four-and-a-bit seasons. Fulfil his contract until 2034 – and avoid expulsion from the league with Manchester City in that time – and he’ll be in with a shout.

As for the terms of that lengthy contract, Haaland is said to be on £525,000 per week. That figure can rise to a whopping £875,000 with bonuses.

Capology doesn’t specify the breakdown of what those bonuses are for, but we imagine a significant portion will be to do with when he scores. Which happens a lot.

You can imagine the conversations when Real Madrid sat down with Vinicius’ reps to sort out his new contract in August.

Something like: “See that £500k+ you’re giving to Mbappe each week? We fancy a bit of that.”

After all he’s done at Madrid so far, Vinicius will have felt entitled to a base salary matching Mbappe’s. Remember, this was a player close to winning the Ballon d’Or himself in 2024.

Now, Vinicius gets the same base salary as Mbappe. His bonuses aren’t quite as big, but still, a possible £813,439 per week isn’t something you’d turn your nose up at. Or a year, for that matter.

And there’s your lot. The next best-paid player in Europe all in, according to Capology, is Jamal Musiala on up to £573,962.

But we’re led to believe Kane has just signed the biggest deal in Bayern’s history, so will presumably be on more than that.

#1455. All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most important positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the big difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he said: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”

It was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery said. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

“Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia shows his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

“We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we showed a really good character.”

And that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

Late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

This will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

Though Savio takes the corner quickly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

Maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

Kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

But it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

The Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher

This is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

This is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

Gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

Villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

Gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

Marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

Tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

Savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his new club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

He gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

Robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

So close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

Huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

Ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

Tonali plays it in for Savio but it’s intercepted by a Villa shirt. It’s played out for Jackson on the left wing to have a run and he gets past van Hecke very easily to reach the edge of the area and take a shot – which goes high and wide.

Unai Emery warned Nicolas Jackson about getting unnecessary bookings yesterday after having to substitute him on a yellow card at half-time last week. 30 seconds into the second half, Jackson got a needless yellow car for stopping a free-kick being quickly taken. Emery pointed straight to his head when it happened.

Savio tries to find Bentancur as he makes a run down the centre of the field. The midfielder gets a head on it but it heads the wrong way.

But the game is opening as Spurs push, and Villa go on the counter with Manzambi running down the left side. He feeds a ball through to Jackson who carries it into the box but Kinsky judges it well and comes out to block the shot.

Spurs are pressing very high now and Villa have dropped very deep, especially their midfield.

Savio tries to put a ball in to the box but it’s trapped by Manzambi who plays the ball out. Ruggeri gets the ball back in to midfield to Buendia, who tees up Manzambi for a run into the box. The Swiss international is closed down well though.

Time to see how Spurs will react after that goal.

There’s still plenty of fight left as Kudus sends the ball out to Savio, trying to get to the touchline to cross a ball back in but Ruggeri stays on him.

Spurs: Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus

And as I’m typing this , it’s an early yellow for Jackson for a silly foul. Here we go!

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm

It looks like Mohammed Kudus will be on at half-time for football. He’s been going through his own half-time warm-up. Matt Cash has been doing the same for Villa, so maybe we will see him too.

In all fairness to Spurs, they have pushed for a goal all half and only been denied by some fantastic keeping from Zion Suzuki.

Here are some of the biggest saves of the half:

Zion Suzuki with a double save to deny Spurs an opener 🧤📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/b7WITUtjf2

Back-to-back huge saves from Zion Suzuki! 🤯📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/uXKkicEeer

Predictably, there were boos from the home fans at half-time. That was the ninth half of Premier League football Spurs have failed to score in. They should have done and would have done if it weren’t for the heroics of Zion Suzuki in the Villa goal. Manzambi’s goal was only Villa’s second in the League this season and this is the first time they have led in a League game.

Spurs looking shaky now as they come close to conceding a second, seconds before the whistle finally blows.

Boos around the stadium as the players head down the tunnel. De Zerbi has work to do.

Spurs have not come from behind to win since November 2024.

This is a tall challenge now, as van Hecke is the first to go into the book for a foul on Jackson.

To rub salt in the wound, Spurs have a decent shout for a free kick on the edge of the box before that as Gomes pushes Mateus Fernandes as he makes a run into the box.

Well this is the last thing Spurs would have wanted. Minutes before half-time Manzambi puts the vistors in front.

Robertson slides to try and stop a ball going out for a corner but he only finds McGinn. He sends it into the box and finds Kamara, who takes a shot. It bounces towards goal and Manzambi pokes it past Kinsky for the lead.

Van de Ven is off the pitch on his feet, sporting an impressive bruise now. Spurs are down to 10 as they try to get the swelling down.

There will be five minutes added, though play is yet to resume as van de Ven receives treatment for a cut below his eye.

The last thing Spurs need now is to be forced into another defensive change after losing Porro.

Wan-Bissaka picks up the ball sent out to him on the wing by Manzambi, who is fouled by Marmoush.

The free kick is outside the area, but McGinn takes looking goalwards.

Mings makes the run looking to get his head on it, but van de Ven goes up with him and gets there first to clear it, though the Dutch international takes a blow to the head and goes down for treatment.

Joao Gomes races forward, sending the ball to Ruggeri on his left. He tries to put it in the box, but it goes out the back off Archie Gray for Villa’s first corner.

McGinn delivers but it comes off Solanke, who clears. No luck yet as we head towards half-time, despite plenty of action in front of goal.

Roberston again with a sliding cross that Lindelof sends out the back.

Another corner for Spurs, but it is headed away again by Mings, who gets up high. That’s Spurs’s seventh corner.

Great long ball from Robertson to try and find Marmoush but Suzuki comes far outside his area to control it with his chest on the bounce and play it away with his feet.

Villa get a free kick inside as Bentancur catches Manzambi, but the Swiss international goes down and receives some treatment on the pitch. He has to go off for a minute, but he is on his feet.

But Spurs come again and it’s Tonali this time. He takes a shot from outside the area, and would have beaten Suzuki low on the right, but the shot is just wide.

Spurs get a corner, delivered by Savio, and it’s headed on to Solanke at the back post. He heads it towards goal but it’s blocked by Wan-Bissaka. Cries for handball, but it’s cleared.

Marmoush makes a very well-timed run to get on a long ball from van Hecke, and does well to stay onside. But his first touch is not good enough and Suzuki can come to collect.

Jackson picks up a ball from Kamara, played over him into the Spurs half. He puts it into the centre of the field towards Buendia, who tees up Manzambi but his shot from distance sails over the bar.

Villa now having a spell. Manzambi gets onto a loose ball in midfield and lays it off to Buendia who feeds Jackson in the centre of the field. He does well to keep the ball down and turn round van Hecke to take a shot on the edge of the area, but he skews his shot wide.

He should be hitting the target at least from there but you can see how desperate both sides are to get their noses in front here.

Jackson gets around Gray and runs into the box on the left side. He pokes a ball through to Buendia, who takes a shot on goal at the near post, but Kinsky gets down to his left to stop the shot.

Mings almost causes a catastrophe for Villa as he and Lindelof close a loose ball down. Suzuki comes out to claim, but the defender pokes it towards him, almost past him under pressure and the keeper has to send it out the sideline.

Four huge saves by Suzuki as Spurs have had five early shots in total to Villa’s single shot on target. They are finding a lot of joy against the left side of Villa’s defence.

Fernandes has an attempt from distance, but drags his shot wide.

Well Spurs are really pushing for a goal!

It’s a perfect first involvement for Gray, as he times a perfect run to get behind Ruggeri to pick up a ball from Savio. He lets it run inside the box but it flashes across the face of goal, just tipped away by Suzuki.

Another attempt denied immediately after as Savio connects perfectly with the volley on the edge of the area, and Suzuki dives down to his left to parry away.

Incredible start for the Villa keeper and Spurs can smell a goal coming.

Spurs had started on the front foot, but let’s see how they handle this change.

Porro went straight down the tunnel when he went off. It was a problem with his left leg. That’s a blow for Spurs, as Porro offers an attacking threat.

Early concern for Spurs as Porro has gone down and is looking very frustrated. Archie Gray has gone out to warm up, but this is a huge blow for De Zerbi if Porro has to come off.

He had been missing due to a muscle injury but it’s not clear if that’s the issue here. He has been very good so far today, helping build play and bringing huge amounts of experience.

And a shot on target next for Villa as Manzambi has an effort from just inside the 18-yard box off his left foot, but Kinsky makes a relatively easy save as the ball boucnes towards him.

Villa get their first chance, as Jackson races down the left side but van de Ven is content to stay close and as no Villa players follow him into the box, van Hecke is the one who clears his cross into the box.

Suzuki has been good with his feet since joining Villa, but he’s kicked about three balls straight out of play so far today.

No wonder De Zerbi had his t-shirt pulled over his head. Tottenham looked certain to score their first Premier League goal of the season through Savio. Suzuki didn’t know too much about the first shot, which hit him, but reacted well to tip the second over.

Tonali crosses a great ball in from the left and Savio has two great chances from close range but Suzuki blocks the first with his chest and tips the second over the bar.

The corner, delivered by Savio, is headed out by Mings and Villa keep control.

Suzuki plays a long ball out down the field, and as Jackson and van de Ven tussle to reach it, the defender is shoved to the floor and gets the free kick.

Spurs are putting a lot of pressure on Villa as they try and play the ball out, and McGinn loses the ball again in midfield. Spurs surge forward again but Mings gets his head onto the ball crossed into the box and Villa survive again.

Savio takes but it is headed out. It falls to Porro outside the box who lifts another ball in, but the Villa line holds firm and clears for a throw in from the left side.

Marmoush tries to run into the box but a well-time challenge by Kamara gets the ball off him.

Villa lose the ball in midfield and it’s played up to Solanke. Lindelof comes across well but concedes a corner.

Watch for some long balls from Tyrone Mings down the channels for Nicolas Jackson today. The pair had a little chat before kick-off with Jackson seemingly telling Mings where he wants the ball launched to.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Gray, Bergvall, Kudus.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Gray, Bergvall, Kudus.

Both teams are coming out of the tunnel now, greeted with plenty of noise from the home and away fans.

The stakes are very high for a match so early on the season and kick-off here we come!

This is the second fixture of the week, as Brentford stormed past Chelsea last night 3-0.

Nottingham Forest vs Coventry (Sat 5.30pm)

Led out by the skipper 🫡 pic.twitter.com/5MLh8ZpvU4

It's almost time ⏰#COYS pic.twitter.com/EewgmTnngl

Just heard on TNT that Newcastle have won more games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in 2026 than Tottenham have...

An early goal here for Villa could be catastrophic for the home team.

Neither club have had any players called up for England, but plenty of players will be leaving to join up with their national teams abroad.

From Spurs, Pedro Porro has retained his place in Spain’s squad. Both Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke have been called up for the Netherlands and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky will join the Czech Republic squad, still awaiting his first senior cap.

Among the Villa players to receive call-ups, Johan Manzambi will be leaving to join the Switzerland squad, while captain John McGinn has been called up for Scotland once again. Zion Suzuki will leave to join Japan in the three-week break as well.

No Mathys Tel in the Spurs squad. De Zerbi has given him plenty of chances, but Tel has always been one of the first players the head coach has criticised this season.

"I don't see any player that would strike fear into me."Steven Gerrard and Glenn Hoddle give their thoughts on Spurs' transfer business and current squad 💰🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eM22XDDAjs

Who is the superstar that Spurs need? Join the conversation and let us know who you think is the missing piece in the comments section.

“We have to improve in everything, because like I said, after the game we conceded the first goal in a bad way, because we knew what was the plan in the defensive phase. One long ball on Gakpo is not enough to concede a goal. Also the second goal could have closed Gakpo better and stronger, and the third goal is an individual skill of Szoboszlai.

“We can improve in the qualities of the play. I think we created more chances than the other games, also because Liverpool played with more courage.

“There was more space to attack, to make one-to-one, but I have experience enough to say that sometimes when you are the coach of the team, without you knowing the reason, you are able to score, you can score. And other times, another situation where I think you are playing well, not fantastic, but well enough to score, enough to win, and you don’t win.

“You have to stay calm, to be confident in what you are doing, what the players are doing. They have my full confidence. We move on and we keep going to be better day by day, but not by words, but by fact.”

“Similar, like us, but their potential is a huge potential. They signed, spending, a lot of very good players, but they need as well, time to get compact everything and to achieve understanding their idea.

“Of course, (Roberto) De Zerbi, he’s a fantastic manager. He played fantastic football here and performed fantastic here in Brighton. He did a fantastic job before as well, in Shakhtar, and in Italy, and after Brighton, a fantastic job in Marseille.

“And now, when I can watch them, they are in this process, but of course, they are getting better, they compete fantastic, even losing against Liverpool.

“Of course, being very, very demanding defensively for us, trying to impose and dominate our moment with the ball as well during the game. This is the challenge. Of course, Tottenham, I expect them to be in the top four.”

Two changes for Villa from the side that lost to Nottingham Forest, with Johan Manzambi and Joao Gomes entering the mix. It’s a first full debut for Manzambi since joining the club from Freiburg over the summer. Gomes returns having served his suspension following a red card against Brighton on the opening weekend.

Representing Aston Villa ✊ pic.twitter.com/5xnjiPnRny

Only one change from the team that faced Everton, as Pedro Porro returns to the starting XI, replacing Archie Gray. Carabao Cup goal-scorer Connor Gallagher is on the bench.

Our Spurs side to face Villa 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Xgpl4Hx9VV

Good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side currently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

But before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!
